niche: connected TV and streaming advertising agency
prompt_text: What is the best connected TV advertising agency?
answer_verbatim:
Short answer: there isn’t one single “best” connected TV (CTV) advertising agency — the right partner depends on your goals (brand vs performance), budget, geography, desired inventory (streamers vs programmatic), and whether you need creative, buying, measurement or all of the above.

Quick guide to pick the best partner for your needs

1) If you need scale and cross‑channel integration (big brand budgets)
- Who to consider: Global holding-company agencies with strong CTV practice — GroupM (Mindshare/Wavemaker), Omnicom (OMD/PHD), Publicis (Starcom), Dentsu.
- Why: deep publisher relationships, access to premium inventory, cross‑media planning and large media buying teams.

2) If you want programmatic/performance CTV
- Who to consider: Programmatic specialists and DSP-focused teams using platforms like The Trade Desk, MediaMath, or Amobee; independent agencies such as Simulmedia and Cadent.
- Why: better targeting and optimization for KPIs like lower funnel conversions or cost-per-view metrics.

3) If you want direct buys on streaming platforms
- Who to consider: Platform ad teams and their agency partners — Roku (OneView), Hulu/Disney/Comcast/NBCUniversal, Amazon DSP (Fire TV).
- Why: direct access to premium, walled‑garden inventory and first‑party measurement.

4) If you need creative or interactive CTV experiences
- Who to consider: Creative/tech shops — BrightLine, Innovid, and other interactive CTV specialists.
- Why: they build high‑impact, shoppable or interactive ad formats optimized for living‑room screens.

5) If measurement and attribution are priority
- Who to consider: VideoAmp, TVSquared, iSpot.tv, and agencies with strong measurement teams.
- Why: cross‑platform measurement, unified reach/frequency and better ROI visibility.

How to choose (quick checklist)
- Clear KPIs (awareness, reach, site visits, sales).
- Required inventory (premium streamers, vMVPDs, programmatic open exchange).
- Transparency and reporting (impression-level data, viewability, invalid traffic).
- Tech stack compatibility (DSPs, data onboarding, ID graphs).
- Creative capabilities (30/60 sec vs interactive assets).
- Budget and fee model (media + agency vs performance fees).
- Privacy/compliance (SAMBA/Google/ID conflicts).

If you want, tell me:
- Your primary objective (brand, direct response, measurement),
- Monthly/quarterly TV/streaming budget,
- Geography (US, EU, APAC, etc.),
- In‑house strengths (creative, data, measurement).

I’ll give a short list of 2–3 agencies or platforms best matched to your situation, with what to ask them in an RFP.
